subject: Follow-up: demo recap, recommended evals, and urgent pin request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@citizenpay.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@citizenpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: model recommendations + eval pack

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call today — great to get a view into CitizenPay’s normalization pipeline and the two main problem areas: (1) transaction description normalization (strict correctness) and (2) edge-case anonymized merchant names (precision over recall). Quick recap and concrete next steps below.

What I’m attaching: citizenpay_eval_pack_20261107.zip — contains:
- curated prompt sets (50 canonical prompts + 120 edge cases)
- eval harness (script + sample input)
- baseline golden outputs and scoring rubric (precision / hallucination checks)

Model recommendations (based on latency & cost targets you shared):
- redwood-4k-v1 @ default float: best balance of factuality for long contexts (recommended for normalization task).
- redwood-compact-q4: cheaper option; useful for lower-cost bulk embedding / fallback but expect slightly more brevity and occasional omission.
- pin strategy: start with redwood-4k-v1 for the canonical eval set; evaluate compact in parallel for throughput testing.

Benchmarks & docs: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/financial-nlp-2026 (includes the scoring script and comparative charts).

Suggested next steps:
1) You run the eval pack against your anonymized sample set (we included the scoring harness).
2) Share the top 20 failures (by severity) — we’ll triage and propose prompt tweaks + a recommended model flag.
3) If the eval shows regression vs your current baseline, we’ll propose a pin/rollback plan and a short A/B to validate.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync on Tue 2026-11-10 10:00 PT to review initial results. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

I’m cc’ing Marissa from Solutions so she can jump in on rollout/pinning logistics once you’re comfortable.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: citizenpay_eval_pack_20261107.zip
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@citizenpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@citizenpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model recommendations + eval pack

Aditya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the pack. We ran the harness this morning against ~2k real anonymized rows and compared redwood-4k-v1 (current prod) against the most recent default variant that your team rolled out on 2026-10-29. We’re seeing a notable uptick in hallucination-like normalizations on merchant names — incorrect expansion of abbreviations and a few invented vendor descriptors that weren’t present in input.

I attached a small sample (sample_regression_snippets.txt) showing 12 examples where the newer variant diverged from our baseline and introduced incorrect entities (this is the top-of-stack severity). For context, our QA team polled a small set of delayed transactions and flagged a 4.1% increase in normalization failures on critical fields which would fail our downstream reconciliation.

This is high impact — can Redwood pin us back to the previous model version while we triage? We’d prefer not to route users to an option that regresses core correctness. Please advise ASAP; we can jump on a call.

— Elena
Head of Product, Data Platforms
CitizenPay

Attachment: sample_regression_snippets.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@citizenpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model recommendations + eval pack

Aditya / Marissa —

Thanks for flagging, Elena — helpful sample. Quick technical read: there was a kernel & quantization selection change in the 2026-10-29 rollout that trades a small amount of factual stability for improved latency on very long sequences. In many cases it’s safe, but for strict normalization (where token expansion must match a canonical form) that optimization can increase spurious expansions.

Immediate recommendation (if customer-facing correctness is degraded):
1) Emergency pin: route CitizenPay’s traffic to redwood-4k-v1@2026-10-21 (the last known-good variant) while we triage the quantization path. Pin preserves the current serving runtime + KV cache behavior.
2) Create a canary route for the 2026-10-29 variant with stricter prompt wrappers (forced canonicalization prompts) to reduce hallucination on merchant normalization.
3) Run a targeted diff on the output with the provided eval pack and our internal regression tools. I recommend running the absolute-fidelity checker in the harness.

I’ve attached the internal rollback/runbook excerpt that ops should follow for a pin: slo_rollback_plan.pdf. Ops note: pinning will not change your model API key; it’s a routing override. Expected mitigation time: ~20–45 minutes from request (assuming no infra backfill).

I’m available to join an urgent triage call.

— Rishi
Staff Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: sLO_rollback_plan.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: infra-ops@redwood.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-08T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: URGENT: pin request for CitizenPay (CP-2026-57) — redwood-4k-v1@2026-10-21

Hi Ops —

Customer: CitizenPay (deal CP-2026-57). Priority: P1 customer-facing regression. Requesting an emergency routing pin for their API key(s) to redwood-4k-v1@2026-10-21 per Rishi’s recommendation.

What we need from infra-ops:
- Apply routing override to pin CitizenPay’s production API key(s) to redwood-4k-v1@2026-10-21 immediately.
- Confirm once pin is in place and provide expected timeline to re-run the customer eval (I’ll coordinate).
- If any rollout artifacts block pin, please escalate to on-call infra lead and notify me.

Context & links:
- Deal: CP-2026-57 (high-touch rollout; procurement complete)
- Eval pack link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/financial-nlp-2026 (scoring harness in the zip)
- Internal rollback runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/model-rollback

Elena — I’ll confirm with infra and update you within 30 minutes. If you’re available for a quick 15-minute triage at 11:30 PT I’ll put a hold on your calendar.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
